Specify starting values

Source: R/utility_functions.R
get_startvals.Rd

get_startvals() can be used to obtain starting values for bvar(). If you want to specify your own starting values, it is recommended to first run get_startvals(), and then adapt the resulting bayesianVARs_startvals object accordingly.

Usage

get_startvals(
  prior_phi,
  prior_sigma,
  intercept,
  data = NULL,
  nobs = nrow(data)
)

Arguments

prior_phi

bayesianVARs_prior_phi object. Best use constructor specify_prior_phi().

prior_sigma

bayesianVARs_prior_sigma object. Best use constructor specify_prior_sigma().

intercept

single logical or numeric indicating whether a constant term (intercept) will be included. In case of numeric input, a value of 0 is interpreted as FALSE and a positive non-zero value as TRUE.

data

Optional. Data matrix.

nobs

single integer, indicating the number of observations of data.

Value

Object of class bayesianVARs_startvals.

Examples

# Access a subset of the usmacro_growth dataset
data <- usmacro_growth[,c("GDPC1", "CPIAUCSL", "FEDFUNDS")]

# Specify priors
prior_phi <- specify_prior_phi(data, lags = 1L)
prior_sigma <- specify_prior_sigma(data, quiet = TRUE)

# Get starting values
startvals <- get_startvals(prior_phi, prior_sigma, intercept = 10, data = data)
# Estimate a model
mod <- bvar(data, lags = 1L, prior_intercept = 10, draws = 10L, burnin = 0L, 
            startvals = startvals, quiet = TRUE)
